chunks: He was asked about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.
And know that whatever you gain of anything, then indeed one-fifth of it is for Allah, and for the Messenger, and for the near relatives.
So it was said to him: “Then what belonged to Allah, for whom is it?” He said: “For the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, and what belonged to the Messenger of Allah, then it is for the Imam.”

Then it was said to him: “What do you see if one category among the categories is more and another category is less—what is done with it?” He said: “That is up to the Imam. Have you seen how the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله used to act? Was it not that he only gave according to what he saw? Likewise is the Imam.”

key_terms.الْأَصْنَافِ: the categories or classes among whom distribution is made
key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: the divinely designated authority who administers the share
key_terms.خُمُسَهُ: its one-fifth share due as khums
key_terms.عَلَى مَا يَرَى: according to what he judges appropriate
key_terms.لِذِي الْقُرْبَى: the share designated for the near relatives
key_terms.لِلرَّسُولِ: the portion belonging to the Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله

ai.seo_question: Who administers and distributes khums according to the verse and Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This report explains the meaning of the khums verse by stating that the share ascribed to Allah returns to the Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله, and the Messenger’s share belongs to the Imam عليه السلام. It also establishes that the distribution among the entitled categories is left to the judgment of the Imam, following the model of the Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله.
